name: Film and video production
one_line: A production as an organising whole — its script, preproduction paperwork, shoot media, edit projects, cuts, delivery masters and release-rights records — from development through publication.

deterministic: A screenplay structure with scene headings such as INT./EXT., character cues above dialogue and explicit transitions, especially when paired with a named production or a production-paperwork neighbour.

A preproduction packet containing a labelled call sheet or shooting schedule with a shoot date, call time, location, scene or shot references, and cast/crew roles; a budget or stripboard may support the same production group.
A production-media neighbourhood containing camera-original or take-numbered video/audio files plus a slate, shot list, or camera report that names the production or shoot day.
A non-linear editing or compositing project whose timeline/bins reference a recoverable set of production media, alongside exports or cuts sharing a production stem.

A release package containing a delivery master or named cut plus caption/subtitle, poster/trailer, delivery specification, or handoff manifest; a signed model, property, music, or location release can provide the rights-to-release stage.

The complete lifecycle is a graph/grouping pattern, not a licence to copy a production fact onto every member: script → preproduction → shoot → edit → release/rights is supported only when the individual links are explicit or reviewable.
needs_llm: Deciding whether a script, schedule, media card dump, edit project and delivery export are one production when titles differ or the production name is abbreviated.

Distinguishing a documentary, commercial, music video, short film, social cut or event recording from a generic video file when the work type is expressed only in prose or a sparse project neighbourhood.
Resolving whether a release document authorises filming, a particular use, a territory, a term, or final publication; a signature alone does not establish the scope of rights.
Separating an independent trailer, portfolio reel, stock clip, lecture recording or phone video from a production's own edit when no script, schedule, project file, or rights record anchors it.
Judging whether an archive is a complete handoff, an in-progress backup, or a camera-card copy when its manifest is mixed or partly unreadable.
never_alone: An .mp4, .mov, .mxf, .wav, .aaf, .fcpxml, .prproj, .drp, .srt or .zip extension by itself; extensions route extraction and do not establish a production.
A filename token such as FILM, MOVIE, CUT, MASTER, FINAL, PICTURE_LOCK, ROLL_03, TAKE_07 or DELIVERY without a production-specific neighbourhood.

A camera-original file, duration, codec, resolution, timecode, slate number, or high-bitrate media file alone; the same observations occur in personal videos, lectures, surveillance, stock footage and phone captures.
A script-like document with no production identity; screenplay structure can be a writing sample, classroom exercise, theatre script, or an unrelated draft.
A client, studio, broadcaster, label or festival name alone; organisations may be commissioner, rights holder, venue, subject, sender, employer or merely mentioned.
A calendar event, contact card, email thread, download session, or folder named Production/Film/Video by itself; these are context or retrieval clues, not activation proof.
FINAL, APPROVED, RELEASED or PICTURE LOCK in a filename as proof of approval, delivery or publication; those claims require labelled content or an explicit rights/handoff record.
The absence of a release form, script, metadata, or EXIF as proof that a video is unreleased, personal, or screen-originated.

work_types: schedule, call sheet or shot list
camera original, take or sync audio
rough cut, picture lock or review cut
delivery master, trailer or social cut
model, property, music or location release
grouping_reasons: one named production across its screenplay, treatment and development material
one production's preproduction packet across schedule, call sheet, budget, shot list and crew paperwork
one shoot day or camera-media batch linked by slate, scene, take, timecode, location or production name
one edit project and the media, proxies, captions, audio stems and exports it references
one review or delivery cycle across cut, notes, responding cut, master and handoff manifest
one release-rights packet whose releases, licences and permissions govern the production or its intended publication
the lifecycle is intentionally cross-format and cross-stage; membership must be evidenced per file rather than propagated from a single script or folder

template.why: Empty by contract: the creative schema declares no field rows, so this placeholder may recommend recognition and grouping but may not branch on project, stage, artifact_type or a film-specific synonym. The lifecycle belongs in accepted groups and work-type values: script → preproduction → shoot → edit → release/rights. If creative fields are ratified later, the natural recommendation would be project → stage → artifact_type, with film stages and media forms as values; a production-stage-first tree would scatter the same work across script, shoot and edit. Time is not first: shoot dates and release dates are distinct observations, and capture-first organization belongs to the photos/capture situation.

must_not_conclude: that the script is approved or financed

must_not_conclude: that the date is the only production date

that attendees are cast or crew without role evidence

archive paths share a production stem

must_not_conclude: that every archive member is approved for every territory

file_examples.filename: Model release - Mara Chen - Harbour Lights.pdf
observations: signed form names a person, production, permitted media and a usage territory
term and signature dates are labelled

must_not_conclude: that all footage featuring the person is cleared
that the license covers an unlisted sequel, territory or medium

observations: curated reel combines excerpts from several unrelated works
opening slate names a director and portfolio URL
no script, schedule, edit project or production rights packet is present
must_not_conclude: that the director owns rights to every excerpt

collides_with.signal: A curated director reel or selected-works export can look like a production delivery, but portfolio framing and multiple unrelated works indicate career material rather than one production.

An editing project or media archive can contain structured project files and manifests, but a production timeline and referenced media are not a software repository; repository markers and source files support code instead.

Camera-origin video and stills can share capture metadata and shoot-day context; a film production requires screenplay, production paperwork, timeline or rights evidence, while a photo event can activate from capture/event evidence.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone script, cut, release, or media file with durable purpose but no recoverable production group should remain independent rather than receive a synthetic film branch.
An ambiguous cut, schedule, rights email, or mixed archive whose production membership or release status cannot be resolved needs review.
Downloaded trailers, stock footage and visual references with no current production anchor are retrieval material, not production members.
Signed releases and contact-bearing rights records may need protected local handling even when production association is unresolved.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased scripts, cast and crew contact details, location information, rough cuts, client instructions, music permissions and model/property releases can expose people, production security, contractual terms or embargoed work. The posture follows the production group; this row does not assign a P7 handling class.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: whether the product should expose script, preproduction, shoot, edit and release/rights as a typed lifecycle view in the graph. Recommended: keep them as work_type/stage values and explicit file edges under the creative schema, with no film-specific fields or child nodes. A later field-ratification decision could adopt project → stage → artifact_type, but this placeholder must not decide that schema change.
